prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The official rate limits for the GitHub REST API depend on whether the request is authenticated or unauthenticated. For unauthenticated requests, the limit is significantly lower to prevent abuse, while authenticated requests (using a personal access token or OAuth) receive a higher allowance based on the user's account status.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests using Basic Authentication or OAuth, you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests via Basic Auth or OAuth are limited to 5,000 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For GitHub Enterprise Cloud, the rate limit for authenticated requests is 15,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests on GitHub Enterprise Cloud are limited to 15,000 requests per hour.
